scope: ID resolution plus specific official-wording shortfalls. This is not a new independent learning/science review of all 81 designs.

findings.type: audit convention warning does not hold against current official source
findings.finding: The audit says the 2025 torque point uses cosine. Current NESA MathML and its aria-label specify sine, consistent with the design's area-normal angle. A change to cosine is not required by this official point.

officialPoints.text: Analyse the factors that affect the magnitude of torque on a current-carrying loop using τ=nIA_(⊥)B=nIABsinθ

findings.type: mapped point is only partly taught
findings.finding: The official point requires four paths: masses in uniform gravity, satellites, charges in electric fields and moving charges in magnetic fields. The design compares satellites and electric/magnetic cases; the uniform-gravity mass case is not a full four-way comparison. Retain a partial match, not full-point coverage.

officialPoints.text: Account for the similarities and differences between the paths of masses in uniform gravitational fields, satellites in orbit, charged particles in electric fields, and moving charged particles in magnetic fields

findings.type: mapped point is only partly taught
findings.finding: The official point includes both DC and AC motors, split rings and slip rings. This design teaches the split-ring DC motor and smoothing, not the complete AC/slip-ring part. Retain a partial match.

officialPoints.text: Analyse the structure and function of the components of simple direct current (DC) motors and simple alternating current (AC) motors, including rotor coils, field magnets, brushes, and split-ring commutators and slip rings

findings.type: mapped points are only partly taught
findings.finding: Both official points include thermionic emission. This design teaches photoelectric graphs and calculations without thermionic-emission experiments or problems. Retain the photoelectric part; the full-point match does not hold.

officialPoints.text: Analyse data from photoelectric effect and thermionic emission experiments to explain relationships using K_(max)=hf-ϕ and K_(max)=qV_(0)
Solve problems involving the photoelectric effect and thermionic emission using K_(max)=hf-ϕ and K_(max)=qV_(0)
